lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide is the event. The company's own documents lean it to meet or beat the ~25-27bn NP bar: its FY26 initial guide (16.5bn) sat above its own mid-term path (15bn); the 2026-07-06 FAQ says Dubai profits slipped from FY26 into FY27 and that the FY29 50bn NP target will not be revised; Q3 inventory was 89bn against 53bn at FY25-end; and the 10-01 pipeline lists 11 hotel openings in calendar 2027. The offset is that the 09-17 revision credits 'sale timing brought forward' in hotels, so some FY27 profit landed in FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two prior full-year prints carrying a new-year guide moved +20.89% (2024-10-03) and +8.57% (2025-10-03) close to close (Yahoo chart). The FY26 upward revision gapped +8.2% on 2026-09-18 and closed only +3.06%.

findings.finding: The dividend is the second item at this print. The FY26 forecast of 165 yen was left unchanged at the 09-17 revision, a 24.4% payout on revised EPS of 676.5. Since FY23 payout has run 23-31%, and DPS rose +41% (FY25) and +37.5% (FY26, split-adjusted). A FY27 dividend guide well above 165 yen, or a small top-up to the FY26 final, is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend has been raised with every full-year print since FY19 (FY25 deck dividend chart). Those prints moved +20.9% and +8.6%, but on guidance; the dividend's share of the move cannot be separated.

findings.finding: The FY26 actual is pre-released: on 2026-09-17 the company raised FY26 to sales 163.7bn, OP 27.6bn, ordinary profit 25.7bn, NP 16.6bn (from 150/26.5/24.0/16.5). IFIS consensus still reads ordinary profit 24.7bn, so the reported year can only confirm the revision, plus or minus a small rounding beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The revision itself moved the stock +3.06% close to close on 2026-09-18, after an +8.2% open. Kabutan's 09-18 note says consensus had sat at the old plan.

findings.finding: Prime-broker shorts of ~7.4% (MS, Barclays, JPM, UBS, BNP, Mizuho) were flat to slightly covering into the print (MS -0.13pp, UBS -0.03pp on 09-30). A guide that clears the bar has buy-to-cover behind it, though part of the position is plausibly a hedge against the 22bn CB.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable. The 2024 full-year print (+20.9%) is consistent with a squeeze, but the register is not on file for that date.

outside_window.finding: Dilution overhang. Last year a 34.5bn public offering followed the full-year print by three weeks (stock -15.17% on 2025-10-27). The Q3 balance sheet shows long-term debt up 15.8bn and a 22bn CB, and the company has launched US projects (Miami, Las Vegas, Dallas), a data centre and an M&A strategy. Another raise is plausible but has no date, and if it came it would most likely land after the window.

The strongest positive the release could carry is a HELD FY forecast backed by the September recovery (+3.1% same-store sales). I looked for buybacks and dividend changes and found no precedent at H1 prints. A hold would be a relief rally from PBR 0.76, which is why p_up sits at 43 and not lower.

findings.finding: Q2 (Jun-Aug) sales slowed sharply. Same-store sales ran 96.8/98.9/101.9 against 103.8-106.3 in Q1, and all-store sales ran 102.9/104.9/107.5 against about 111.5. Q1 SG&A grew 15.0% on 11.7% sales growth. Together these put H1 OP near ¥2.75-3.25bn against the ¥3.8bn H1 plan, which needed Q2 OP up about 20.6% YoY on the prior year's ¥1,966m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-06): OP -5.1%, progress 37.6% against a 5-year average of 44.1% (kabutan); stock -4.61% the next session. H1 FY26 (2025-10-06), on plan at 59.1% progress: -1.34%.

findings.finding: If H1 lands near ¥3.0bn OP, the FY OP plan of ¥5.52bn (+4.4%) needs H2 OP of about ¥2.5bn, against ¥1.815bn last year and the plan's own implied ¥1.72bn. A full-year cut, probably to 'one-turn' profit decline (一転減益), is likely with this release. Last fiscal year the company cut FY OP by 10% together with its Q3 results, and it has revised at an H1 print before (2023-10-05).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-01-06 FY cut released with Q3 (OP ¥5,750m -> ¥5,155m, 一転減益): -4.15% the next session; kabutan/minkabu ran '大幅反落'. 2023-10-05 a revision came with H1 (direction not confirmed): +4.21%.

findings.finding: September same-store sales were +3.1% (customers -0.4%, spend +3.5%) and all-store sales +8.5%, the strongest month since May. This gives management an H2 recovery story to set against the H1 miss. The English version is dated Oct 5 and appeared on kabutan at 10:05 JST. The Japanese 月次 normally goes out at 15:30 with the results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August 月次 (same-store sales +1.9%, first positive in three months) produced +0.61% the next session and three straight up days (kabutan 2026-09-07). The July 月次 produced +1.06%.

findings.finding: A disclosed institutional seller is still distributing. Fidelity and its joint holders fell from 10.0% to 9.96% by 2026-07-15 and from 9.96% to 9.13% (1,965,638 -> 1,802,738 shares) by 2026-09-15, with FMR UK cutting from 6.47% to 5.13%. Retail margin longs are 12-30x the margin shorts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five consecutive post-print sessions were negative (2025-07-04 -5.0, 2025-10-06 -1.34, 2026-01-06 -4.15, 2026-04-06 -3.65, 2026-07-06 -4.61), computed from Yahoo daily closes.

findings.finding: The stock trades at PER 7.65 (forecast) and PBR 0.76 at ¥1,586 (2026-10-02), the bottom of its 2020-2026 ranges (7.6-19.68x and 0.76-2.48x), and near the 2026 low of ¥1,570. A FY cut to about EPS ¥175 still leaves it under 9x, so the release is a candidate for 悪材料出尽くし (the bad news is out).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2025 FY print came at a then-low of ¥1,636 and rose +8.19% (Yahoo closes 2025-04-07 -> 04-08); that is the only large positive reaction in the last eight.

outside_window.finding: Q3 (Sep-Nov) recovery, if the September +3.1% same-store sales trend holds, would show up in the January 2027 Q3 print and the monthly reports from November.

lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on public 月次 or 進捗率): the visible H1-miss finding moved from -0.7 to -0.3 and p_up from 40 to 43. The FY-cut finding was left at -1.5 because a cut is something the release ADDS, which rule 1 exempts.

Rule 2 (check the sign): wrote the strongest positive (a held forecast plus the September recovery) into baseline_tension. I had already looked for returns, so the positive findings were left unchanged.
Open question 4 (a 5-day run-in as a signal): not used; the -4% 5-day run-up was not sized as its own finding.
